title: Bank Deposit Notice Credit for Promptly Reported Incorrect Amounts
content:
A customer who reports a Bank Deposit incorrect amount promptly earns a notice credit in the make-good credit Paloma puts into the transfer. Promptness is counted in calendar days from the transfer's date of availability to the date of the incorrect-amount notice on the transfer's case file.

## The rule

An incorrect-amount notice given no more than 7 calendar days after the date of availability earns the prompt notice credit of 1.50 US dollars; one given later but no more than 30 calendar days after it earns the timely notice credit of 0.75 US dollars; any later notice earns no notice credit.

## Questions and answers

**What counts as day zero?** The date of availability itself. A notice on that date is 0 days after it.

**A notice on the 7th day after the date of availability?** 1.50; seven days is no more than 7.

**On the 8th day?** 0.75.

**On the 30th day?** 0.75; thirty days is no more than 30.

**On the 31st day?** No notice credit.

**Does the notice credit depend on the size of the shortfall?** No. It is a fixed dollar amount set only by how promptly the notice was given.

| Days from the date of availability to the notice | Notice credit |
|---|---|
| 0 to 7 | 1.50 |
| 8 to 30 | 0.75 |
| 31 or more | none |
